stories.title: The Path to a Democratic Supermajority
stories.take: Adam Jentleson's plan: stop playing for 50-plus-one — compete in all 50 states, run state-fitting candidates under a big tent with no litmus tests, and over-focus on affordability • Democrats are on track for 56 Senate seats and 250–260 House seats; his target is 62 Senate seats by 2029 • Abolish the filibuster, he argues, so a majority can actually govern — and members from red states can break away without killing bills • Don't repeat 2009: spend political capital fast on shared ground like expanding health care toward universal coverage

stories.title: How US model agencies helped Epstein access victims
stories.take: The answer: a BBC investigation found agency MC2 sponsored models' visas and sent them to Epstein's Florida mansion after his conviction — president Jeff Fuller appears 200+ times in the DOJ files, emailed Epstein about models, and booked a flight for Rosa weeks after she says Epstein first abused her • A New York trafficking bill would let police investigate enablers who knew or should have known • Also: Hegseth calls his impeachment push 'sabotage' as a vote looms, U.S.–Russia–Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi, and Russia's Novaya Gazeta closes after 30 years

stories.title: The Jensen Huang Affair
stories.take: Stephen Witt's three revelations: the affair itself, Megaspede allegedly funneling Nvidia chips to China via Malaysia, and the Trump administration knowing for about a year • Huang has no successor — about 60 people report directly to him — so this is key-man risk for the whole U.S. market • Witt expects the board won't fire him; the real risk is congressional hearings, liability, and his credibility on China policy dropping to zero • Malaysia took 10–15% of Nvidia revenue despite no big local AI program

stories.title: How to Make Journalism Fun, with Maury Povich
stories.take: The answer: take stupid things seriously and follow the money — a bankruptcy filing listing KL2 Aspire, LLC owed $7 million, with no public Kawhi Leonard–Aspiration link, opened the Clippers investigation • Melt the cheese on the broccoli: use the sports story people love to carry race, money, power and ethics underneath • Fallout Torre cites: Clippers lost five first-round picks, Ballmer suspended a year, Leonard fined $700,000, with federal probes continuing • Do it as a group project, vet hard with a lawyer, and treat truth as armor

stories.title: Scandal At Nvidia: Is This The End For Jensen Huang?
stories.take: The answer: no settled verdict — Ashley Gold says Congress would push Huang out but the board, bound to shareholders, keeps him; Robert Armstrong bets it is 'impossible to come back from' as solo CEO and predicts Huang moves to chair with a new CEO • Both guests expect stronger export controls regardless • Huang admitted the affair in a letter to staff; Megaspede bought nearly $5 billion in Nvidia chips in 2024; Nvidia shares closed down 4% • Markets rallied anyway — S&P and Dow up over 2%, Nasdaq up 3%

stories.title: Secrets, Chips and Spycraft: The Nvidia C.E.O. Scandal
stories.take: Megaspede bought over $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips in about two years and became a poster child for the Southeast Asia loophole around China export bans • U.S. intelligence assessed executive Alice Wong as a Chinese Ministry of State Security asset; Trump was briefed about a year ago and took no action, and Huang was never warned • Huang admitted the affair to staff over the weekend; the board opened an independent investigation while Trump defended him • Incoming Senate Banking Chair Elizabeth Warren oversees chip exports — hearings loom in January

stories.title: Where did all the sitcoms go?
stories.take: The answer: streaming killed the syndication payoff — sitcoms once lost money on air, then profited at 100 episodes; streamers pay less for long terms • Streamers order 8–10 episodes instead of 22, so fixed costs like a $3 million set crush per-episode economics • Comedy doesn't travel overseas and streamers count minutes watched, making an hour drama worth twice a sitcom • Sitcoms fell from about 12% of new shows in the 1990s to under 2% in the 2020s

stories.title: LA City Council race is closer than ever, Where Raman beat Bass, Horvath vs Barger over LA County CEO— Morning Edition

stories.title: Hegseth Impeachment Push, Trump Holds Off Iran Strikes, Congress Summons Nvidia's CEO
stories.take: Hegseth faces eight impeachment articles, mostly over waging war without Congress; removal would still need 67 senators • Trump holds off Iran strikes, calling the war effectively over and the status quo fine — while admitting war-driven prices hurt Republicans at the midterms • Three House committees summoned Jensen Huang to a closed-door session; Nvidia slipped about 4.25% while AMD rose over 13% • Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised and backs Huang for now

stories.title: Investors Weigh Fallout from Nvidia Spy Scandal
stories.take: Washington fallout: China is the one bipartisan issue, so the Nvidia spy scandal likely brings tougher chip export laws — even though one expert argues AI can't be contained and controls may accelerate Beijing's independence • Markets took it in stride, piling back into tech after last week's sell-off; Anthropic still plans to list before Thanksgiving • California voters rejected the one-time 5% billionaire tax • U.S. drug-price pressure has cut new European drug launches 27% in 17 months
